messages:
maria: FYI support ticket INC-1731 from AcmePayments. They report sudden p95/p99 spikes on hosted text.generate around 2026-03-15T09:20Z. p95 jumped from ~130ms to ~520ms, p99 to ~1.8s. Users seeing intermittent timeouts. They included a short log fragment and say this started when traffic had short bursts (~40rps bursts for 3-4m).

aj: thanks, can you paste the log + which model/route? any infra deploys during the window?

maria: route=text.generate model=redwood/gpt-medium-open hosted. No deploy-bot events in that timeframe (deploy-bot: no deploys). Customer logs:

```
[2026-03-15T09:21:02Z] req=aa1 route=text.generate queued_in_batch=9 wait_ms=595 flushed_by=timeout
[2026-03-15T09:21:02Z] req=bb2 route=text.generate queued_in_batch=1 wait_ms=610 flushed_by=timeout
[2026-03-15T09:21:02Z] req=cc3 route=text.generate queued_in_batch=10 wait_ms=12 flushed_by=size
```

maria: they called out the second line where a single request sat ~610ms.

nish: that looks like the continuous batcher is holding small singletons until max_wait_ms+some jitter. Which batcher config is serving that shard?

kevin: pulling config for hosted-pool-shard-7: continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=10, continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=600, adaptive=false.

nish: that explains it. With max_wait_ms=600 we will see singletons wait ~600ms before flush when arrivals are sparse or bursty. Under bursty traffic you can get a lot of these timeout-flush events and tail latency spikes. CPU/GPU usage is low, so this is a batching artifact.

aj: short-term mitigation: reduce max_wait_ms for this tenant (or route-level override) and lower max_batch_size so small flows don't wait. We can do a canary to verify impact.

maria: customer asked for a quick fix, and also wants repro steps so they can validate on their side.

nish: proposed quick steps:
1) apply a tenant-scoped config: max_wait_ms=60, max_batch_size=5 on the routing shard serving AcmePayments.
2) canary 10% traffic for 5m, measure p95/p99.
3) if good, roll to 100% and monitor for cost impact.

kevin: small note: reducing wait will slightly increase per-request cost (less batching) but should drop p95/p99 significantly. I can add an alert and short-lived dashboard for this tenant.

aj: go ahead and run the canary. nish, please prepare rollback commands.

nish: scripting it now. commands below:

```
# start canary
redwoodctl apply-config --tenant=acme-payments --pool=hosted-pool-shard-7 --set continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=60 --set continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=5 --canary 10 --note "INC-1731 latency mitigation"

# revert
redwoodctl revert-config --tenant=acme-payments --pool=hosted-pool-shard-7 --to-prior --force
```

deploy-bot: canary rollout started at 1769460060 (10% traffic)

kevin: early telemetry after 3m on canary:
- canary p50 95ms, p95 110ms, p99 310ms
- control p95 515ms
- cost per request up ~7% on canary

maria: customer checked canary endpoint and reported much improved interactive latency on their end.

aj: after validation we rolled to 100% at 1769460120. Post-roll metrics (observed 10m after roll):
- p50 stable ~100ms
- p95 improved from ~520ms -> 115ms
- p99 improved from ~1.8s -> 340ms
- overall throughput unchanged, GPU utilization low, batching occupancy decreased.

nish: quick RCA notes: continuous batcher tuned aggressively for throughput (max_wait_ms=600) but under bursty, uneven arrivals single requests wait to hit size threshold and flush on timeout, causing long tail. KV cache hit rate for this workload was low so caching didn't help.

nish: longer-term fixes to avoid manual toggles:
- implement adaptive batching that lowers max_wait_ms when latency SLOs breach or queue depths are low
- per-route service-level defaults (latency-sensitive routes get smaller wait_ms by default)
- expose tenant/route overrides in Console with safety checks and suggested defaults
- add CI e2e synthetic that simulates bursty small-token traffic and fails PRs that degrade p95/p99

kevin: I'll add a dashboard tile for tenant-specific batch_wait histogram and a playbook link to the runbook. Also will create an alert: if route p95 > 300ms for 5m -> page eng-sre.

aj: action items:
- aj: monitor the tenant for 24h and confirm stability (assigned) 
- nish: write RFC for adaptive batching + simulation results, include cost/latency tradeoffs (due EOW)
- kevin: dashboard + alert for tenant-level batch wait + runbook (due 48h)
- maria: update INC-1731 and coordinate billing note with finance (likely small delta) then close after 24h stable (due +1d)

sophia: from AcmePayments: thanks y'all. latencies are back to normal for our users. appreciate the fast help :raised_hands:

aj: great. we'll follow up with the RCA + RFC in #postmortems once nish has the doc. closing this thread but keeping incident ticket open for 24h observation. :white_check_mark:
